```{python}
#| include: false
import pandas as pd
import plotly.graph_objects as go
from IPython.display import HTML
from twinfault_site import *

month = last_full_month()
prev = (pd.Timestamp(month + "-01") - pd.DateOffset(months=1)).strftime("%Y-%m")
m = sql(f"""
    select month,
           sum(direct_calls) as calls,
           sum(failed_calls) as failed,
           sum(failed_calls) / sum(direct_calls) as rate,
           median(median_fee_eth) as fee
    from fct_daily_token_health
    where month in ('{month}', '{prev}')
    group by month
""").set_index("month")
cur, old = m.loc[month], m.loc[prev]
since = f"vs {month_label(prev)}"
points = (cur.rate - old.rate) * 100
```

## Row {height=190px}

::: {.valuebox icon="x-octagon" color="#fdecee"}

`{python} f"{cur.rate:.2%}"`

`{python} small(cur.fee)`

`{python} change(cur.fee, old.fee)` `{python} since` (median of daily medians)
:::

## Row {height=420px}

```{python}
#| title: Daily failure rate of direct calls (7-day average)
health = sql("""
    select h.date, h.token, h.direct_calls, h.failed_calls, h.median_fee_eth, p.avg_base_fee_gwei
    from fct_daily_token_health as h
    left join fct_daily_pipeline as p using (date)
    order by h.date
""")
fig = go.Figure()
for token in TOKENS:
    d = health[health.token == token].set_index("date")
    rate = d.failed_calls.rolling(7, min_periods=1).sum() / d.direct_calls.rolling(7, min_periods=1).sum()
    fig.add_scatter(x=rate.index, y=rate.values, name=token, mode="lines",
                    line=dict(color=TOKEN_COLORS[token], width=2), hovertemplate="%{y:.2%}")
fig.update_yaxes(tickformat=".1%", rangemode="tozero")
show(fig)
```

```{python}
#| title: Failed direct calls per month
monthly = sql("""
    select month, token, sum(failed_calls) as failed
    from fct_daily_token_health group by all order by month
""")
fig = go.Figure()
for token in TOKENS:
    d = monthly[monthly.token == token]
    fig.add_bar(x=d.month, y=d.failed, name=token, marker_color=TOKEN_COLORS[token],
                hovertemplate="%{y:,.0f}")
fig.update_layout(barmode="stack", bargap=0.15)
fig.update_yaxes(tickformat="~s")
show(fig)
```

## Row {height=420px}

```{python}
#| title: Typical fee per direct call (daily median, ETH, log scale)
fig = go.Figure()
for token in TOKENS:
    d = health[health.token == token].set_index("date").median_fee_eth.rolling(7, min_periods=1).median()
    fig.add_scatter(x=d.index, y=d.values, name=token, mode="lines",
                    line=dict(color=TOKEN_COLORS[token], width=2), hovertemplate="%{y:.3g} ETH")
fig.update_yaxes(type="log", tickformat=".1~e")
show(fig)
```

```{python}
#| title: Failure rate vs network base fee (one dot per day; ρ = rank correlation)
fig = go.Figure()
for token in TOKENS:
    d = health[(health.token == token) & (health.direct_calls >= 500)].copy()
    d["rate"] = d.failed_calls / d.direct_calls
    rho = d[["avg_base_fee_gwei", "rate"]].corr(method="spearman").iloc[0, 1]
    fig.add_scatter(x=d.avg_base_fee_gwei, y=d.rate, name=f"{token} (ρ = {rho:.2f})", mode="markers",
                    marker=dict(color=TOKEN_COLORS[token], size=5, opacity=0.55),
                    customdata=d.date.astype(str),
                    hovertemplate="%{customdata}<br>base fee %{x:.2f} gwei<br>failure rate %{y:.2%}<extra></extra>")
fig.update_layout(hovermode="closest")
fig.update_xaxes(type="log", title_text="average base fee that day (gwei)", showgrid=True, gridcolor=GRID,
                 tickvals=[0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200, 500])
fig.update_yaxes(tickformat=".1%")
show(fig)
```

```{python}
#| title: Unusual days for the failure rate, with the pipeline verdict for that day
days = unusual_days(
    "select date, token, failure_rate from fct_daily_token_health where direct_calls >= 500",
    "failure_rate",
)
table = pd.DataFrame({
    "Day": days.date.dt.strftime("%a %d %b %Y"),
    "Token": days.segment,
    "Failure rate": days.value.map("{:.2%}".format),
    "Usual": days.usual.map("{:.2%}".format),
    "Score": days.score.map("{:+.1f}".format),
    "Pipeline that day": days.pipeline.map(pill),
})
HTML(html_table(table, numeric=("Failure rate", "Usual", "Score")))
```

```{python}
#| title: How to read this
HTML("""
<p><b>Usual</b> is the median failure rate on the same weekday over the previous eight weeks.
<b>Score</b> is the gap divided by a robust spread (1.4826 × the median absolute deviation),
so ±4 is roughly four standard deviations and is unlikely to be noise.</p>
<p><b>Pipeline that day</b> comes from the <a href="data-health.html">data health</a> checks.
If it is not OK, the move may be a data problem, not a change in behaviour, and should be
checked before anyone explains it. That question is what the twinfault benchmark tests.</p>
<p class="note">Failed transactions emit no transfer events, so failures are only visible in the
transactions table, from calls sent straight to the token contracts. Days with fewer than 500
direct calls for a token are left out.</p>
""")
```
